findings.title: Backup-code login can bypass password verification
findings.body: The new backup-code branch is entered whenever `credentials.backupCode` is present, but the password check above only runs when `user.password && !credentials.totpCode`. This branch never validates `credentials.totpCode`, so an attacker who knows a valid backup code can POST credentials containing the victim email, the backup code, and any arbitrary non-empty `totpCode` (for example `000000`) without the password. Password verification is skipped, the backup code is accepted, and the attacker is logged in. A backup code must not replace the password factor; verify the password whenever backupCode is supplied, or explicitly validate only the selected factor while still requiring the password.

findings.title: One-time backup codes can be reused concurrently
findings.body: Consuming a backup code is implemented as a read-modify-write of the encrypted backup-code array: the request reads `user.backupCodes`, finds the matching index, sets that element to null, and writes the entire array back. Two concurrent login requests using the same code can both read the original array and both write their own nulled copy, so both requests succeed and the supposedly single-use code is accepted twice. Use a transaction/row lock or an atomic conditional update keyed on the ciphertext that was read so only one request can consume a given code.

findings.title: Closing backup-codes screen via dialog X skips onEnable and loses codes
findings.body: After `handleEnable` succeeds, 2FA is already enabled on the server and the modal switches to `DisplayBackupCodes`. Only the explicit Close button calls `onEnable()` and `resetState()`. Closing via the dialog's X, Escape, or outside click calls `onOpenChange` directly, so the settings switch is not updated, the component can reopen on the stale backup-codes step, and the user may leave without ever seeing or saving the only copy of the backup codes. Any dismissal while on `DisplayBackupCodes` should either commit the enable state and reset state, or be blocked until the user confirms they have saved the codes.

findings.title: No coverage for actual backup-code login, consumption, or disable flow
findings.body: The added e2e assertions only check that the download has the expected filename and that a copy-success toast appears; the file contents and clipboard contents are explicitly left as TODO. There is no test that logs in with a backup code, rejects an invalid code, verifies a used code cannot be reused, or disables 2FA using a backup code. These are the security-critical paths added by this PR, and a regression in code formatting, one-time consumption, or either server endpoint would currently pass the tests.

findings.title: Copy button shows success toast even when clipboard write fails
findings.body: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` returns a promise that can reject when clipboard permission is denied or the API is unavailable, but the promise is neither awaited nor caught and the success toast is shown unconditionally. Users can be told the backup codes were copied when nothing was copied, or an unhandled rejection can be produced. Await the clipboard write and show the success toast only after it resolves, with an error fallback.

findings.title: Password visibility toggle is ineffective after switching to PasswordField
findings.body: `PasswordField` sets its own `type` based on `isPasswordVisible` before spreading `{...props}`, so passing `type="password"` here overrides that dynamic value. Clicking the eye button changes the visibility state but the input remains `type="password"`, making the newly added visibility control non-functional in the enable-2FA modal. Remove the explicit `type` prop when using `PasswordField`, or change `PasswordField` so caller props cannot override its visibility-driven type.

findings.title: Password visibility toggle removed from keyboard navigation
findings.body: Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the password visibility button removes it from the keyboard tab order. Keyboard-only users can no longer focus the control to reveal or re-hide the password, which is an accessibility regression for every `PasswordField` in the application. Keep the button focusable, or provide an equivalent keyboard-accessible way to toggle visibility.
